newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault profits skid in 1996 first half.
newsitem.headline: Renault profits skid in 1996 first half.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA said on Tuesday its profit shrank in the first half of 1996 to less than a tenth of the year-earlier level as car sales fell and a fierce price war eroded its profit margins.
Its net attributable profit dwindled to 158 million francs ($30.80 million) from 1.76 billion in the first half of 1995.
It plunged into a first-half operating loss of 225 million francs, compared with a year-earlier operating profit of 1.52 billion.
The results reflected continuing losses at Renault's car division as well as a slowdown in the trucks unit, which until recently had compensated for the car division's troubles.

The car operation lost 911 million francs, compared with a profit of 358 million a year ago. The division, which rolled into the red in the second half of 1995, has run a deficit of 2.36 billion francs over the past 12 months.
Operating income at Renault's truck division, which includes Mack Trucks of the United States, fell to 26 million francs in the first half of 1996 from 519 million francs.
Only its finance division showed an improvement, reporting a rise in operating income to 660 million francs from 638 million.

The results were roughly in line with expectations from analysts, who view Renault as the most vulnerable of Europe's Big Six carmakers in a tough climate of slow sales growth, fierce competition and price-slashing.
Renault's sales fell to 94.09 billion francs in the first half of 1996 from 96.21 billion, while its share of the European car market fell to 9.7 percent from 10.6 percent last year.

The company's outlook for the rest of the year was grim, the company said. It expects only a slight improvement in the performance of its car division from the second half of 1995, when it lost 1.35 billion francs, while the truck unit is likely to show an operating loss.
"In France...in a context characterised by sluggish consumer spending and a very acute sensitivity to prices, the automobile market should remain strong in the third quarter," it said.
"But there is a risk of a significant decline in the fourth quarter," it added.
"Under these conditions, operating income of the automobile division would only show a slight improvement compared with the second half of 1995."
The end of the third quarter coincides with the expiry on September 30 of a government incentive scheme to persuade people to replace their old cars.

"In the area of commercial vehicles, Renault will have to contend with the combination of a continued downturn in the cycle in the United States and marked slowing in the European markets. Consequently, the operating income of the commercial vehicles division would be negative," the company said.

Renault, which formally entered the private sector in July when the French state reduced its participation to below 50 percent, last year launched the new mid-sized Megane car to boost its profits and market share.
But analysts said the new car hit a crowded market as Renault's rivals moved faster to renew their model ranges in light of the fiercely competitive environment.

Renault has also been hurt by its head-to-head rivalry with Italy's Fiat, which also specialises in small cars and has benefited greatly from the lira's weakness relative to the franc and other European currencies.
